import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# Data cleaning and preparation
# Fill NaN values in 'Sleep Disorder' for consistency, though not used in this specific plot
df['Sleep Disorder'] = df['Sleep Disorder'].fillna('No Disorder')

# Unify 'Normal' and 'Normal-Weight' BMI categories
df['BMI Category'] = df['BMI Category'].replace('Normal-Weight', 'Normal Weight')

# Define a specific order for BMI Categories for better visualization
bmi_category_order = ['Normal Weight', 'Overweight', 'Obese']
# Ensure 'BMI Category' is a categorical type with the desired order
df['BMI Category'] = pd.Categorical(df['BMI Category'], categories=bmi_category_order, ordered=True)


# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure with two subplots to compare Sleep Duration and Quality
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(16, 6), sharex=True, sharey=False) # sharey=False as scales are different

# Plot 1: Average Sleep Duration by Stress Level, colored by BMI Category
sns.pointplot(data=df, x='Stress Level', y='Sleep Duration', hue='BMI Category',
              hue_order=bmi_category_order,
              errorbar='se', capsize=0.1, ax=axes[0], palette='viridis')
axes[0].set_title('Average Sleep Duration by Stress Level and BMI Category', fontsize=14)
axes[0].set_xlabel('Stress Level (Higher = More Stress)', fontsize=12)
axes[0].set_ylabel('Average Sleep Duration (hours)', fontsize=12)
axes[0].legend(title='BMI Category', loc='lower left', bbox_to_anchor=(0.0, 0.0))
axes[0].tick_params(axis='x', labelsize=10)
axes[0].tick_params(axis='y', labelsize=10)

# Plot 2: Average Quality of Sleep by Stress Level, colored by BMI Category
sns.pointplot(data=df, x='Stress Level', y='Quality of Sleep', hue='BMI Category',
              hue_order=bmi_category_order,
              errorbar='se', capsize=0.1, ax=axes[1], palette='viridis')
axes[1].set_title('Average Quality of Sleep by Stress Level and BMI Category', fontsize=14)
axes[1].set_xlabel('Stress Level (Higher = More Stress)', fontsize=12)
axes[1].set_ylabel('Average Quality of Sleep (1-10, Higher = Better)', fontsize=12)
axes[1].legend(title='BMI Category', loc='lower left', bbox_to_anchor=(0.0, 0.0))
axes[1].tick_params(axis='x', labelsize=10)
axes[1].tick_params(axis='y', labelsize=10)

# Add a super title for the entire figure
fig.suptitle('Impact of Stress Level and BMI on Sleep Health', fontsize=16, y=1.03)

# Adjust layout to prevent overlapping titles/labels
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.98]) # Adjust rect to make space for suptitle

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
